Title: January
acf_description: January on St. Croix brings brings the most anticipated event of the year, Crucian Christmas Festival. The Crucian Christmas Festival starts in December but culminates in January with the children's parade and the adult parade, the latter being the most anticipated event of the Crucian carnival season.  The Christmas winds and perfect weather also provide the ideal setting for many outdoor events, including the Krewe de Barkus Dog Parade, the Dolphins Sea Swim, and the St. Croix Scenic 50 ultra-marathon. You can also continue to enjoy a few of the recurring monthly events such as Art Thursday in Christiansted, outdoor movies and Caribbean Community Theatre productions. Find out about all this and more below!  More About January on St. Croix: These events typically take place each January here on St. Croix, but the dates will vary so check out our Calendar of Events for details: Crucian Christmas Festival: Food Arts & Crafts Fair, Crucian Christmas Festival: J'ourvet, Crucian Christmas Festival: Children's Parade, Crucian Christmas Festival: Adult Parade, Three Kings Mile Race, Dolphins Sea Swim, St. Croix Scenic 50, Art Thursday, Caribbean Community Theatre Show, Krewe de Barkus Dog Parade, Fort-to-Fort Run.  January Holidays: New Year's Day (31st), MLK Day (3rd Monday)  Average Temperatures: The average daily temperatures in January range from the low 70s to low 80s (°F), with strong breezes from the Christmas winds  Average Rainfall: January is part of the drier season on St. Croix, averaging about 0.5 inches of rain  Local Seafood in Season: Caribbean Spiny Lobster, Conch, Mahi, Wahoo, Tuna  Seasonal Wildlife to Watch For: Humpback whales migrate along St. Croix during the late winter months, sometimes as early as late January. There are also occasional sights of whale sharks and manta rays.  Migratory Birds to Watch For: Black-necked Stilt, Blue-winged Teal, Great Blue Heron, and Northern Waterthrush migrate to the Virgin Islands for the winter months.

Title: February
acf_description: February brings comfortable, drier weather to St. Croix making it the perfect time for St. Croix to host the agricultural festival in the Territory, AgriFest. This weekend long cultural festival is a celebration and exhibition of local produce, livestock and and handmade products attended by visitors and exhibitors from around the Caribbean. February also brings one of Christiansted's four annual Jump Ups, the North Shore's Mardi Croix Parade and the annual Orchid Show at the St. George Village Botanical Garden. You can also continue to enjoy a few of the recurring monthly events such as Art Thursday in live music at the fort in Christiansted, and outdoor moves. Find out about all this and more below! More About February on St. Croix: These events typically take place each January here on St. Croix, but the dates will vary so check out our Calendar of Events for details: Jump Up, Mardi Croix, Agrifest, Art Thursday, Rhythms at Sunset, Caribbean Community Theatre Show. High Season: February is part of the high (or peak) tourism season on St. Croix. While St. Croix isn't really a place with big crowds, February is a busier time on the island. More things are open, and there are lots of things to do, but make reservations for restaurants, tours and attractions whenever possible.  February Holidays: Valentine's Day (14th), Presidents' Day (3rd Monday).  Average Temperatures: The average daily temperatures in February range from the low 70s to low 80s (°F).  Average Rainfall: February is part of the drier season on St. Croix, averaging about 0.4 inches of rain.  Local Seafood in Season: Caribbean Spiny Lobster, Conch, Mahi, Wahoo, Tuna.  Local Fruits in Season: Soursop, coconut, papaya, banana, pineapple, passionfruit, watermelon, sugar cane, noni.  Seasonal Flowers + Blooming Plants: Red hot poker vine bloom this time of year with beautiful, showy, crimson flowers with yellow or orange on the outside of the petals. Bromeliads, including pineapple, also bloom this time of year.  Seasonal Wildlife to Watch For: Humpback whales migrate along St. Croix during the late winter months. There are also occasional sights of whale sharks and manta rays.  Migratory Birds to Watch For: Black-necked Stilt, Blue-winged Teal, Great Blue Heron, and Northern Waterthrush migrate to the Virgin Islands for the winter months.

Title: March
acf_description: March is a great time to be on St. Croix. With beautiful weather and lots of sunshine comes lots of events and things to do, most notably the St. Patrick's Day Parade!  Held in Christiansted, this parade is full of festive floats, live music, dancing and the quintessential mocko jumbies. You can also enjoy other outdoor events like activities like the Christiansted Vintage and Collectibles Fair, road races and sporting events. On a cultural note, March 31st is Transfer Day which commemorates the day that the Danish West Indies were formally ceded to the United States by Denmark, thus becoming the US Virgin Islands.  Find out about all this and more below! More About March on St. Croix: High Season: March is part of the high (or peak) tourism season on St. Croix. While St. Croix isn't really a place with big crowds, March is a busier time on the island. More things are open, and there are lots of things to do, but make reservations for restaurants, tours and attractions whenever possible.  March Holidays: St. Patrick's Day (17th), Transfer Day (31st), Easter Sunday (may be March or April).  Average Temperatures: The average daily temperatures in March range from the high 70s to mid-80s (°F). Average Rainfall: March is part of the drier season on St. Croix, averaging about 0.5 inches of rain. What rain showers there are most often on the light side and pass by quickly. Local Seafood in Season: Caribbean Spiny Lobster, Conch, Mahi, Wahoo, Tuna.  Local Fruits in Season: Soursop, coconut, papaya, banana, pineapple, passionfruit, watermelon, sugar cane, noni. Seasonal Flowers + Blooming Plants: Century plants bloom in early spring to late summer with clusters of bright yellow flowers. The South American cannonball tree is also in bloom, with fragrant red flowers and giant cannonball fruits.  Seasonal Wildlife to Watch For: Humpback whales migrate along St. Croix during the late winter months. There are also occasional sights of whale sharks and manta rays.  Migratory Birds to Watch For: Black-necked Stilt, Blue-winged Teal, Great Blue Heron, and Northern Waterthrush migrate to the Virgin Islands for the winter months.

Title: April
acf_description: As winter fades and spring is reborn, it is a beautiful time of year in St. Croix! Temperatures range from the mid-70’s to the mid-80’s and there are only 7 days of rain on average, making April one of St. Croix's sunniest and coolest months. So, the islanders take advantage of the nice weather to host a variety of annual events in April. How about participating in an a more athletic activity such as the Golden Hook Dolphin Fishing Tournament? If you would prefer to enjoy the arts, stroll through charming downtown Christiansted and enjoy Art Thursday. Don’t forget, April 22 is Earth Day! Consider celebrating Earth Day by enjoying one of the eco-friendly activities St. Croix has to offer. High Season: April is part of the high (or peak) tourism season on St. Croix. While St. Croix isn't really a place with big crowds, April is a busier time on the island. More things are open, and there are lots of things to do, but make reservations for restaurants, tours and attractions whenever possible.  April Holidays: Easter Sunday (sometimes in March), Earth Day (22). Average Temperatures: The average daily temperatures in April range from the high 70s to mid-80s (°F).  Average Rainfall: April is part of the drier season on St. Croix, averaging about 0.5 inches of rain. What rain showers there are most often on the light side and pass by quickly. The South American cannonball tree is also in bloom, with fragrant red flowers and giant cannonball fruits.  Seasonal Wildlife to Watch For: Humpback whales migrate along St. Croix during the late winter months. There are also occasional sights of whale sharks and manta rays.  Migratory Birds to Watch For: Black-necked Stilt, Blue-winged Teal, Great Blue Heron, and Northern Waterthrush migrate to the Virgin Islands for the winter months.

Title: May
acf_description: With an average temperature in the low-80's, May is a great month for outdoor fitness activities on St. Croix, and the island offers many! From the annual Kite Festival hosted by St. Croix East End Marine Park, to VI Triathlon Federation's Mermaid Mixer, there's outdoor fun to be had for all. You can also enjoy some of the many smaller events held at local restaurants and resorts to celebrate this month's Cinco de Mayo and Mother's Day holidays.  Off Season: May is part of the off (or slow) tourism season on St. Croix. While St. Croix isn't really a place with big crowds, May is an especially laid-back time on the island. For many restaurants and storefronts, this is the final month of season and close toward the end of the month, so make reservations for restaurants, tours and attractions whenever possible.  May Holidays: Cinco de Mayo, Mother's Day (2nd Sunday), Memorial Day (Last Monday).  Average Temperatures: The average daily temperatures in May range from the high 70s to mid-80s (°F).  Average Rainfall: May is part of the drier season on St. Croix, averaging about 9 days of rain. What rain showers there are most often on the light side and pass by quickly.  Local Seafood in Season: Caribbean Spiny Lobster, Conch, Mahi, Wahoo, Tuna, White Marlin, Dolphin Fish, Kingfish.  Local Fruits in Season: Custard Apple, Carambola, Dragonfruit, Jackfruit, Papaya, Hog Plum.  Seasonal Flowers + Blooming Plants: Century plants bloom in early spring to late summer with clusters of bright yellow flowers. The South American cannonball tree is also in bloom, with fragrant red flowers and giant cannonball fruits.  Seasonal Wildlife to Watch For: Humpback whales migrate along St. Croix during the late winter months. There are also occasional sights of whale sharks and manta rays. Migratory Birds to Watch For: Black-necked Stilt, Blue-winged Teal, Great Blue Heron, and Northern Waterthrush migrate to the Virgin Islands for the winter months.

Title: June
acf_description: June begins a warming trend for St. Croix bringing temperatures into the high-80's, but the tropical breezes and warm turquoise waters inspire many Caribbean weddings here in June. Graduations and Father's Day events bring families and friends together to celebrate with beach barbecues or special events offered by the local resorts and restaurants. June is a great month for family events here on St. Croix!As is the case with many of the months here on St. Croix, June also offers some great outdoor fitness events. Bring the family out and participate in the 2 Mile annual Women's Race or the 1 Mile Olympic Day Race. If you prefer your events on the water, you can support a great cause by participating in the Kayak for Kids event.You can also continue to enjoy a few of the recurring monthly events such as Rhythms at Sunset in Frederiksted, and Movies at the Fort in Christiansted.

Title: July
acf_description: July continues the warm weather with highs in the high-80's, so many Crucians spend their time in the beautiful blue waters of the Caribbean or lounging around the pool. The 4th of July is celebrated on St. Croix with a stunning fireworks display after the sunsets in Frederiksted. July also offers one of Christiansted's four annual Jump Up celebrations which line the streets of the historic town with vendors, food and live music as well as a parade and mocko jumbies.  July celebrates Mango Melee, the delicious namesake tropical fruit with games, contests and vendors at the beautiful St. George Village Botanical Gardens.You can also continue to enjoy a few of the recurring monthly events such as Rhythms at Sunset in Frederiksted.

Title: August
acf_description: In August things slow way down in St. Croix. With temperatures sometimes climbing to 90 degrees, you're time will be best spent limin' at the beach, floating in the clear Caribbean Sea or in the pool, snorkeling or diving! While there are only a few events on St. Croix in August, you can continue to enjoy some of the recurring monthly events such as Rhytms at Sunset in Frederiksted.

Title: September
acf_description: September on St. Croix can be very warm, with temperatures continuing into the high-80's or 90's, but that doesn't mean there isn't fun to be had on the island this month! What better place to spend Labor Day weekend then limin' on the beach or floating in the warm tropical waters? There are several guided hikes this time of year to some off the beaten path places. Or, you can participate in one of the three annual fitness events held in September on St. Croix: the Labor Day 5K Race, the Virgin Islands 10K Race, or the Wall 2 Wall Sprint Triathlon. Whether you prefer to be active, or take it easy, there's something for everyone on St. Croix.

Title: October
acf_description: While October can be a little warm on St. Croix with temperatures still rising into the high-80’s, it also brings return of the cruise ships to the island. Halloween is celebrated island-wide with costume contests and special events at local establishments. But, the big event for St. Croix this month is the annual Coral Reef Swim. For those that prefer running to swimming, October also boasts the West Indies 5K run. The island can be a little slow in October, so relax and enjoy before the winter holidays are upon you!

Title: November
acf_description: November is an activity-filled month on St. Croix! With temperatures cooling down slightly so the highs are in the mid-80's, the year's biggest holiday season kicks off and the athletes come out for several different events like the Coral Reef Swim Race. After you enjoy Thanksgiving, soak up some local culture and start your holiday shopping at the Christmas Jump Up (St. Croix's Black Friday in Christiansted) or Starving Artist Day. Looking for something a little more active? The St. Croix International Regatta, the Golden Hook Fishing Tournament, and the Queen Louise Golf Tournament also happen this month. For the athletes and running enthusiasts out there, November brings the Veteran's 5K run, the Caribbean Classic Triathlon, the Fort to Fort Relay, the Manchester 5M Race and the always popular Mermaid Mixer. So, there is something for the whole family!You can also continue to enjoy a few of the recurring monthly events such as Art Thursday, Sunset Jazz in Frederiksted, Jazz in the Park in Christiansted, and Movies at the Fort in Christiansted. Title: December
acf_description: December 'cools' down with an average temperature of 78 degrees, and the incoming Christmas Winds bring tropical breezes to the island. Even better, December is a festive month to be on St. Croix! Not only are there many Christmas festivals and celebrations throughout the month, but December also kicks off the Crucian Carnival season. Celebrate the Christmas season at the St. George Village Botanical Garden's Garden of Lights, Gallows Bay Holiday or join in the fun of Crucian Carnival by heading out to enjoy some of the pageants or vist one of the festival villages.If you want to help the community this month, participate in the annual Christmas Bird Count, enjoy some local cuisine at Crucian Fusion, or attend the Holiday Hope Benefit. For those looking for something more active during this cooler month, the International Marathon, Half Marathon and Relay Marathon, as well as the Cane Bay 5 Mile Road Race are held this month.You can also continue to enjoy a few of the recurring monthly events such as Art Thursday and Rhythms at Sunset in Frederiksted.
